Thanks Rachel — jumping in with a technical recommendation and short answers for security/procurement. Summary first, details below: 

Recommendation (pilot -> production):
- Pilot: Redwood Dedicated pool (customer-dedicated GPUs) in their cloud region with VPC peering to MedAffinity network. This satisfies day-one PHI isolation and lets us iterate quickly.
- Production (post-pilot): Move to Private (customer-managed control plane + VPC) if they need on-prem or tighter network controls.

Sizing (based on 40 RPS sustained, 120 RPS bursts, average prompt ~60 tokens):
- Baseline Dedicated pool: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs with continuous batching + KV cache (handles sustained 40 RPS comfortably with 99% headroom).
- Burst capacity: autoscale policy to add up to 6x GPUs for short spikes (120 RPS), with pre-warmed instances for predictable burst.
- Notes: exact GPU type and model variant depend on the model they pick and quantization.

Noise-neighbor / isolation controls:
- We provide tenant-dedicated GPU pools (no noisy-neighbor shared compute) for Dedicated customers. For Hosted customers we use strict cgroup-based GPU scheduling, token-bucket QoS, and per-tenant priority queues.
- For further isolation we can enable model sandboxing, limit concurrent generation slots per tenant, and reserve memory quotas to avoid cross-tenant OOMs.
- Operationally: we include telemetry (per-tenant token/latency traces), and automatic eviction/fallback policies to a smaller model variant if a tenant exceeds burst thresholds.

SLO suggestions (short completions):
- p50: <= 60 ms (API response time for streaming-first-token for cached/prefix hits)
- p95: <= 400–600 ms (depending on model and sequence length)
- p99: <= 1200 ms (for large sequences or cold KV misses)
- We can do tighter SLOs for Dedicated pools with pre-warmed instances and prefix caching enabled; Private deployments often yield more consistent tail latency.

Attachments: I’ve attached a quick sizing CSV and a draft mutual action plan (MAP) to use with procurement.

Open questions for pricing/commercial: what margin band should we prepare for Dedicated vs Private? Rachel — happy to sync on pricing once you have the band.

Ben
